If sentiment is positive in the last 3 days and forecast is trending up, reduce the late-period forecast by 1–2% to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is negative in the last 3 days and forecast is trending down, increase the late-period forecast by 1–2% to counteract pessimism.  
If sentiment is neutral and forecast is flat, apply a 0.5–1% upward adjustment in mid-period to capture latent momentum.  
If sentiment spikes to positive after a downward trend, shift forecast midpoint upward by 1–1.5% in the next 5–7 days.  
If sentiment is consistently negative over 5+ days, reduce early-period forecast by 0.5–1.5% to reflect bearish sentiment persistence.  
If sentiment is positive but forecast is over-optimistic (e.g., >10% above recent high), apply a downward correction of 1–2% in the first 3 days.
